algebraic_carriers.maps_to_algebra: field (approximately - true field axioms violated by IEEE-754 rounding; see flaws)
monoid (union with frozenset() identity; approximates boolean_algebra over a finite universe but Python sets are unbounded so complement is not total)

flaws: float-not-field: maps_to_algebra='field' for float is *approximate* - IEEE-754 floats violate associativity (1e20 + 1 - 1e20 != 1) so they're not a field in any rigorous sense. W22 follow-up: introduce an approximation_of_field algebra card and tighten this carrier.

set-not-boolean-algebra: Python sets approximate boolean_algebra over a finite universe but the universe is unbounded so complement (NOT) is not a total operation. Classified as monoid (union) honestly; boolean_algebra would require a finite-universe wrapper card.

GIL-elided: concurrency_model lists threading.Thread without flagging the GIL's impact on parallelism. A future python_gil_axiom card would capture this; for now see the python.py frontend docstring which calls it out explicitly.
version-fluid: minor-version differences (3.9 dict |, 3.10 match, 3.11 except*) not enumerated; this card describes the abstract language ~3.10.
informal_description: Python is a strongly-but-dynamically-typed multi-paradigm language with eager evaluation, permissive side effects, reference-counting GC backed by a generational cycle collector (in CPython), and duck typing for structural compatibility checks. Concurrency is split three ways: native OS threads (constrained by the GIL in CPython so threading helps IO-bound but not CPU-bound code), cooperative async with asyncio for IO concurrency on a single thread, and multiprocessing for true parallelism by spawning OS processes. Python's int is arbitrary-precision and forms a ring under +/*; float approximates a field but is not one (IEEE-754 rounding breaks associativity); str/list/tuple/dict each form a monoid under concatenation or union. The transpile frontend at cards/tool/v_transpile/frontends/python.py uses ast.parse to lift CPython source into the substrate IR; constructs outside the IR's normalised set (e.g. metaclasses, __getattr__ hooks, send/throw on generators) lift opaquely as Raw nodes with structured warnings.
name: python
notes: CPython-centric. PyPy / Jython / GraalPython preserve the language semantics but vary the memory model (PyPy uses a real tracing GC; GraalPython uses the GraalVM GC). The async sub-language (PEP 492) is technically a separate evaluation model layered on top - async functions return coroutine objects and are *not* eagerly evaluated until awaited; we still classify the host language as eager_strict.
